clue.text: Think for ages about such an honour

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the three words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion to ponder for years over receiving some distinguished award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the twelve letters of THINK FOR AGES. In bridge the ace, king, queen, jack and ten are called honours, so a king of hearts is one such card.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as bridge, the top cards of a suit, including each king, are termed honours.

clue.text: Benign cardinal and family

parts.note: benign means kind, gentle
cardinal is a deep red colour, from the robes of cardinals

explanation.surface: A kindly churchman of high rank together with his relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred is a collective term for one's relatives, the people related by blood.

clue.text: Only one is involved in so rowdy a manner

indicators.note: involved suggests something tangled up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A remark that just a single person is caught up in such disorderly behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Done noisily means done with loud clamour, the way a boisterous crowd behaves.

clue.text: Insolent attack

explanation.surface: An abusive, cheeky assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive as an adjective means rude or insulting; as a noun it is a military assault or campaign.

clue.text: Ruth's hiding in old wood

indicators.note: a hiding is a beating, so the letters of the name are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: the name with its possessive S is used as five letters

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth is concealed in an ancient forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' looks like concealment, but it means a thrashing, which scrambles RUTHS. The word in the sense of a wooded hill survives mainly in English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurst is an archaic word for a wooded rise or copse.

clue.text: French-Canadian academician getting rid of mice?

indicators.note: getting rid of says the rodents' letters come out of the scholar's title, the question mark allowing them in any order

explanation.surface: A scholar in the academy who sets about clearing out the rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters E, M, I and C, which spell the rodents in a different order, come out of ACADEMICIAN, leaving the answer. Acadia was the French colony in what is now Nova Scotia and nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: An Acadian is a descendant of the early French settlers of Canada's Maritime region.

clue.text: Oil-change after journey from capital

indicators.note: after places the scrambled oil behind the journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the letters of the word oil

explanation.surface: Changing the oil in a car following a long drive out of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: It displays a light range of colours-one shade contains fantastic scoop!

definitions.text: It displays a light range of colours

indicators.note: contains means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a shade is a ghost, a spectre

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Excitement over a scoop about a colourful light display.
explanation.walkthrough: A shade is a ghost here, not a hue, despite the colours nearby; 'one' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectroscope is an instrument that splits light into its spectrum for examination.

clue.text: Pope parking on row

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a row is a quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: The Holy Father leaving his car alongside a street of terraced houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiff is a title of the Pope, the supreme bishop of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Representational art-style is accepted by kingdom

indicators.note: accepted by means the word is is taken in by the kingdom

parts.note: a kingdom is a realm

explanation.surface: A national art movement depicting life faithfully is endorsed by the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is the artistic approach of depicting subjects truthfully, as they actually appear.

clue.text: Bowler supports cash enterprise that looks promising

indicators.note: supports means in this down entry the bowler sits underneath, holding up the cash

parts.note: cash means money
a spinner is a type of bowler in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler backs a business venture with his own funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' is not a hat: a spinner bowls slow, turning deliveries in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinner is a venture or product likely to bring in lots of profit.

clue.text: Harris endlessly in study of this crow

indicators.note: in places the shortened name inside the study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: endlessly means the name loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone named Harris is researching a particular bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' as a verb, to con, a bookish old word; the bird is named by its diet.
explanation.definitionFit: The carrion crow is a common black crow named for feeding on dead flesh.

clue.text: Old hat displayed by eccentric-or not?

indicators.note: displayed by means the letters can be seen within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dated piece of headgear is worn by someone who may or may not be odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' seems to mean old-fashioned, but it is literally an antique hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat worn in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Blooming healthy

explanation.surface: A flower in fine fettle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddy is a mild British intensifier like bloody or blooming, and also describes a fresh, rosy complexion of good health.

clue.text: Sweep in my time's changed!

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the phrase are put in another order

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep remarks how things have altered in his day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges IN MY TIMES; the sweep is not a chimney cleaner but a wide expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep can be a vast extent, as in the sweep of a plain, which is vastness.

clue.text: Nurseryman's guarded forecast for hawthorn?

explanation.surface: A gardener cautiously predicts whether a hedge plant will bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, it is what a cautious gardener says: it might bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a hedged prediction that a plant could bloom; the second is a folk name for the white-blossomed hawthorn, which flowers in spring.

clue.text: Bashful about a number of games in the bushes?

indicators.note: about means the bashful word goes around the games

parts.note: bashful means shy
a rubber is a series of games, as in bridge or tennis

explanation.surface: A timid person hiding in the undergrowth for a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is a planted area of shrubs, a mass of small woody plants.

clue.text: Oiled, perhaps, in "The Fleet" pub?

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the fleet

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the fleet

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word oiled is a possible rearrangement of the letters we want

explanation.surface: A drunken sailor, well oiled, in a dockside tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' scrambles the word oiled (giving EDLIO) inside the fleet. The Red Lion is the most common pub name in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Lion is a classic name for a British drinking house.

clue.text: Prevent ruler from holding an account

parts.note: to prevent can mean to ban
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Stopping a monarch from opening a bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: Banking is keeping one's money with a bank in an account there.

clue.text: Second humble fellow in Leicester, for example…

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the notoriously 'umble character in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: Another modest chap living in the city of Leicester.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester looks like the English city but is a breed of sheep (Leicester Longwool).
explanation.definitionFit: The Leicester is a long-wool breed of domestic farm animal kept for wool.

clue.text: Grain as milled for Spanish drink?

indicators.note: grain that is milled is ground up, so these letters are broken and reshaped

explanation.surface: Cereal ground to make a Spanish beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and sometimes brandy.

clue.text: Graceful eglantine not in fashion

indicators.note: not says the letters of in are left out of the flower's name
fashion as a verb means to shape, so the remaining letters are remade

explanation.surface: A flower, the sweetbriar, is lovely, though out of vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' removes I and N from EGLANTINE, and 'fashion' rearranges the remaining EGLANTE. 'in fashion' looks like a phrase meaning trendy, but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means stylish and refined, pleasing in form or manner.

clue.text: … the first, perhaps lad in love with redhead?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
the head of red is R

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words lad in can be rearranged into other letters

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired young man falls head over heels, continuing the sheep theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is the first letter of 'red'. The ellipsis links this to the previous clue: Leicester was the example there, 'the first' here.
explanation.definitionFit: First is an ordinal number, marking position in a sequence.

clue.text: Motorway lighted all round as far as one can go

definitions.text: as far as one can go

indicators.note: all round means the lighted word wraps the motorway

parts.note: lighted means lit
Motorway gives MI

explanation.surface: A motorway lit up along its whole length to the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is the furthest point or boundary, beyond which nothing goes.

clue.text: Light carried (in case)

parts.note: a source of light that is taken around inside a protective glazed box, in case it is needed

explanation.surface: Bringing a torch just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp enclosed in a protective casing.

clue.text: Government by top people in house, semi-lit perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of semi-lit may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A dimly lit chamber where the ruling class sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is the belief that power should rest with a select, privileged few.

clue.text: Home of great bed once, holding retired RAFfighting!

indicators.note: holding means the town goes around the other piece

parts.note: the Great Bed of Ware, a huge Elizabethan bed, was once kept in the Hertfordshire town of Ware

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the air force initials are written backwards

explanation.surface: A town where a famous bed stood takes in retired airmen for combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the air force initials round (FAR). Ware is a Hertfordshire town; the Great Bed of Ware is now in the V&A museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare is armed conflict, the waging of combat.

clue.text: Champion away from home?

parts.note: a defender of good causes who wanders far and wide, rather than playing a match on another team's ground

explanation.surface: A sports winner playing an away fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval romance figure rode out in search of adventures, righting wrongs and defending the weak.
